ranking_by: share of dry air by volume
title: The 5 Most Common Gases in the Air, Ranked (Oxygen Isn't #1)

scenes.text: Oxygen is not number one in the air you breathe.

scenes.label: Neon · 0.0018%
scenes.text: Number five: neon. Only about eighteen parts per million of the air, roughly five hundred times rarer than argon.

scenes.label: Carbon dioxide · 0.04%
scenes.text: Number four: carbon dioxide. About zero point zero four percent of the air, yet every plant on Earth depends on it.

scenes.label: Argon · 0.93%
scenes.text: Number three: argon, at nearly one percent. It does almost nothing, yet there's over twenty times more of it than carbon dioxide.

scenes.label: Oxygen · 21%
scenes.text: Number two: oxygen. About twenty-one percent of the air, the part your body actually needs to stay alive.

scenes.label: Nitrogen · 78%
scenes.text: Number one: nitrogen. Seventy-eight percent of every breath, and your lungs push it in and out without using it.

description:
The five most common gases in dry air, ranked by share of volume.
Oxygen only comes second: nitrogen makes up about 78 percent of the air, while oxygen is about 21 percent and argon, a gas that does almost nothing, is third.
Which of these surprised you most?
first_comment: Did you know oxygen was only number two? What should we rank next?
